title: Platform sync — session store migration
note: Synthetic meeting with KNOWN ground truth, used as the shareable sample recording AND as the evaluation fixture. Every line is deliberately chosen to exercise something the rubric scores.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Alright, let's start. Main thing today is the session store. Arjun, where are we?

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: So right now sessions live in Redis, and we're seeing latency spikes on the Kubernetes cluster, about two hundred milliseconds at the ninety fifth percentile.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: It's only on three nodes, but it's enough to hurt the checkout flow.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Is that a Redis problem or a networking problem?

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Mostly Redis. The connection pool thrashes under load. I think we should move the session store to PostgreSQL.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: PostgreSQL will be slower per read, but it's far more predictable, and we already run it in staging.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Okay. Let's do it. We're moving the session store from Redis to PostgreSQL. That's decided.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: While we're at it, maybe we should switch the internal calls from REST API to gRPC. It might help the latency too.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Let's park that one. Interesting, but not this sprint, and I don't want to change two things at once.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Agreed. I'll benchmark the PostgreSQL session store latency and have numbers by Friday.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Good. Sam, can you update the Grafana dashboard so we can actually see the new metrics?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Yes, I'll take the Grafana dashboard.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: And someone needs to document the rollback procedure before we ship anything.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: One more thing. We are not going to do the OAuth migration this sprint. It's blocked on the vendor.

decisions.statement: Move the session store from Redis to PostgreSQL
decisions.evidence: We're moving the session store from Redis to PostgreSQL. That's decided.

decisions.statement: Switch internal calls from REST API to gRPC
decisions.why: TRAP: proposed by Sam, explicitly parked by Priya. A proposal is not a decision.

decisions.statement: Defer the OAuth migration to a later sprint
decisions.why: A legitimate decision our ground truth originally missed - found by gpt-oss-120b, not by qwen3:14b. Recorded as a known recall difference between the two Stage 3 backends rather than scored, since it was discovered after the fixture was written.

action_items.task: Benchmark the PostgreSQL session store latency
action_items.why: Arjun says 'I'll benchmark...': the owner is recoverable only by knowing WHO IS SPEAKING. Without diarization the correct answer is unspecified. With diarization + evidence-based naming it is Arjun, FLAGGED inferred: Priya addresses 'Arjun, where are we?' and that voice answers; the same voice later says 'I'll benchmark'.
owner stated, NO deadline stated - deadline must come back unspecified
TRAP: 'someone needs to' - no owner, no deadline. Both must be unspecified.

must_preserve.negation: We are not going to do the OAuth migration this sprint
must_preserve.why: Stage 2 must not alter numbers or flip the negation.

injections.note: Synthetic TTS pronounces jargon too clearly, so Whisper gets it right and Stage 2 has nothing to do. These verified phonetic corruptions simulate real ASR mis-hearings so the refinement path can actually be measured. Each has been confirmed to match its target under Double Metaphone.

negative_control.why: A NEAR MISS on a real glossary term: 'stage inn' sounds close to 'staging' but does not match under Double Metaphone, and - verified - no sub-span of it matches any glossary term either. It must stay UNCORRECTED. This is what separates a discriminating gate from one that fuzzy-matches anything vaguely similar.
negative_control.previous_control_was_invalid: 'oh auth' for OAuth was correctly rejected as a whole phrase, but its sub-token 'auth' IS a legitimate phonetic match for OAuth, so the n-gram scan corrected that instead and the control could never pass. A valid control must have NO matching sub-span.

speaker_names.why: Arjun and Sam are addressed by name and answer; nobody ever says Priya's name, so her voice must stay an anonymous label rather than be guessed.
